display_name: A Singapore household's income tax and employee CPF for a year of assessment (YA 2026, with income year 2026 as YA 2027): one or two resident adults and their children, composing the Income Tax Act 1947 encoding and the Central Provident Fund Act 1953 encoding
scope: A resident individual or a married couple who are both resident, income year 2025 (YA 2026) or 2026 (YA 2027): wages month by month (ordinary and additional), trade income and rent after their deductions, tax-exempt income for the $8,000 tests; children (qualifying child relief, working mother's child relief, parenthood rebate); the reliefs of s 39 that a household can state; s 39A; the Second Schedule Table 3; the employee's share of CPF under the First Schedule as in force in 2025 and 2026. A foreign employee (neither a citizen nor a permanent resident) is covered with employee CPF nil (Central Provident Fund (Exemption) Order 2018, para 3). Answers NOTHING (not covered): a non-resident adult; a permanent resident in the first two years; any income year but 2025 and 2026 and any year of pay that is not twelve months, for a foreign employee too; a share of a child's relief or rebate that no division could give. Cannot be stated, so not to be used for: employment expenses, donations, taxable pensions in earned income, self-employed CPF, more than one employer, a child under articles, adoption or marriage as the route to a parenthood rebate, the conditions of s 39(2)(c), (d) and (o), the spouse and sibling top-up cliff of s 39(3AA), discretionary remissions, Budget rebates outside the Act's text.

forks.H1: 'income' in the $8,000 tests includes tax-exempt income
forks.H2: the share of each child's qualifying relief, and separately of the parenthood rebate, is an input; a share outside 0 to 1, or not 1 for a sole adult, answers NOTHING
forks.H3: children listed oldest first; a mother's order counts the children within s 39(2)(e), including one whom para 3 or 3B bars from a deduction
forks.H4: a child who turns 16 during the year is 'below 16 at any time'
forks.H5: taxable pensions are not in earned income
forks.H6: results are exact to the cent; the Act has no rounding rule
forks.H7: each spouse may claim for the other
forks.H8: the CPF relief is the employee's share

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Acts.
